newsitem.title: USA: Calif tax measure has major credit impacts-Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Calif tax measure has major credit impacts-Moody's.

text.p: A tax measure approved by California voters in November has significant rating implications but was not expected to be devastating for local government credit, Moody's Investors Service said Thursday.

California's Proposition 218 strengthens existing law to require that all new local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. It also allows property owners to approve new assessments and strictly limit the use of fees and charges.
"While we do not think 218 will be devastating, it may contain one or more ticking time bombs that could, at least temporarily, disrupt a portion of the market," Moody's said.
Moody's said it was reviewing the ratings of the nine largest cities and 10 largest counties in the state.

Moody's said it had completed its reviews for five cities -- lowering ratings for Los Angeles, San Diego, Sacramento, and Fresno while affirming ratings for San Jose. Reviews of the cities of Anaheim, Long Beach, Oakland and Riverside were underway and expected to be completed in the coming weeks.
Moody's said no changes in county ratings were expected and that it has not made any changes in its ratings of revenue bonds, sales tax bonds, Mello-Roos bonds or assessment debt.

Moody's said the most certain and probably the most significant impact of Proposition 218 would be an increase in general fund budget pressures for cities and counties and a reduction in their financial flexibility.
Its rating actions so far have focused on general obligation and general fund debt "because this is the one area where the impact of Proposition 218 is certain."

Downgrades have been focused on cities rather than counties because the new restrictions are most significant for cities, Moody's said, adding that county ratings already reflect their limited financial flexibility.
